title: Lemon sorbet
subtitle: Sharp, intensely flavoured lemon sorbet
excerpt: A clean, sharply flavoured lemon sorbet made from fresh lemon juice and zest in a simple sugar syrup. Dairy-free, intensely refreshing, and the ideal palate cleanser or light dessert.
sourceNotes: Standard lemon sorbet using the simple syrup method. Ratio of juice to sugar syrup calibrated for sharp rather than sweet; cross-referenced with David Lebovitz, The Perfect Scoop (2007).

recipe.freezeNotes: Store for up to 3 months. Sorbet can become very hard; rest at room temperature for 10 minutes before scooping.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The syrup can be made up to 1 week ahead and refrigerated. Churn on the day of serving.

content.text: Lemon sorbet is one of the simplest things to make well. The ratio of lemon juice to sugar syrup determines the balance; this version errs on the sharp side. Use unwaxed lemons for the zest. The sorbet sets harder than ice cream; give it 10 minutes at room temperature before scooping.

items.prepNote: unwaxed; about 250 ml juice and 2 tbsp zest

content.text: Zest 4 of the lemons finely. Juice all 8 lemons. You need 250 ml juice; adjust the number of lemons accordingly.

Combine the sugar and water in a small saucepan. Stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves completely. Do not boil; as soon as it is clear, remove from heat. Add the lemon zest, cover, and leave to infuse for 15 minutes.

Strain the syrup through a fine sieve to remove the zest. Stir in the lemon juice. Taste: it should be quite sharp and slightly over-sweet (freezing dulls sweetness and sharpness equally). Refrigerate until completely cold.
Churn in an ice cream machine for 20 to 25 minutes until thick and pale. Transfer to a lidded container and freeze for at least 2 hours before serving.

items.symptom: The sorbet is icy rather than smooth
items.cause: The base was not cold enough before churning, or sugar ratio is off
items.fix: Chill the base overnight. Adding a tablespoon of liquid glucose helps prevent ice crystals.

items.symptom: The flavour is flat and not lemony
items.cause: Zest not steeped long enough or poor lemon quality
items.fix: Infuse the zest in the warm syrup for at least 20 minutes. Use unwaxed lemons with fragrant zest.

items.cause: Ratio shifted too far toward syrup
items.fix: Add more lemon juice before churning. Taste the base: it should seem almost too sharp.

items.symptom: The sorbet has turned to solid ice in the freezer
items.fix: Rest at room temperature for 10 minutes. If very solid, cut into pieces and re-blend briefly to restore texture.

content.text: Lemon sorbet has two roles at the dinner table: as a light dessert in its own right, and as the palate cleanser served between courses at formal dinners. The Italian tradition serves it in a scooped-out lemon shell (sorbet di limone), sometimes with a little limoncello poured over. The French serve it in a chilled glass with a leaf of mint. Both are excellent. It is also the component in the classic 1970s dinner party pudding: scooped into champagne glasses with a measure of prosecco poured over at the table.
